} from './fixtures.ts'

const phase = verificationPhase()

const projectsUrl = '/projects'
const projectUrl = (projectId: string) => `/projects/${encodeURIComponent(projectId)}`
const workflowUrl = (projectId: string, workflowId: string) => `${projectUrl(projectId)}/workflows/${encodeURIComponent(workflowId)}`
const runUrl = (runId: string, nodeId?: string) => `${workflowUrl(PROJECT.project_id, WORKFLOW_ID)}/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}${nodeId ? `/nodes/${encodeURIComponent(nodeId)}` : ''}`
const apiRun = (runId: string) => `/api/projects/${PROJECT.project_id}/workflows/${WORKFLOW_ID}/runs/${runId}`

const rootsNav = (page: Page) => page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Roots' })
const workspace = (page: Page) => page.getByTestId('projects-workspace')
const graphNode = (page: Page, nodeId: string) => page.locator(`[data-testid="workflow-graph"] [data-graph-node="${nodeId}"]`)
const nodeListItem = (page: Page, nodeId: string) => page.locator(`[data-testid="run-node-list"] [data-node-id="${nodeId}"]`)
const nodeDetail = (page: Page) => page.getByTestId('node-detail')

/** No view action may launch, approve, retry, delete or edit a run: no such real controls exist (graph nodes are read-only selectors). */
async function expectNoExecutionControls(page: Page) {
  const controls = workspace(page).locator('button, input, select, textarea, [role="menuitem"]')
  await expect(controls.filter({ hasText: /approve|retry|launch|start|resume|delete|cancel|integrate|edit|save/i })).toHaveCount(0)
  await expect(page.locator('form')).toHaveCount(0)
}

async function attach(page: Page, testInfo: TestInfo, id: string) {
  const image = testInfo.outputPath(`${id}.png`)
  await page.screenshot({ path: image, fullPage: true })
  await testInfo.attach(`screenshot:${id}`, { path: image, contentType: 'image/png' })
}

async function waitForProjectsApi(request: APIRequestContext) {
  if (phase !== 'candidate') return
  await expect.poll(async () => (await request.get('/api/projects')).status(), { timeout: 30_000 }).toBe(200)
}

  await waitForApi(request)
  await waitForProjectsApi(request)
  if (phase === 'worker') await installProjectMocks(page)
})

test(`[scenario:projects-navigation] Pi and Claude remain usable and Projects opens registered projects (${phase})`, async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  // The existing skills graph still loads at Home with only the two sources, and the roots strip offers Projects.

  await expect(rootsNav(page).getByRole('link')).toHaveText(['Pi', 'Claude', 'Projects'])
  await expect(page.locator('.graph-canvas .node')).toHaveCount(2)
  await expect(page.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'File operations' })).toBeVisible()

  // Projects opens the registered project list without disturbing the skills domain.
  await rootsNav(page).getByRole('link', { name: 'Projects' }).click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/projects$/)
  await expect(currentCrumb(page)).toHaveText('Projects')
  await expect(rootsNav(page).getByRole('link', { name: 'Projects' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-current', 'page')
  const list = page.getByTestId('projects-list')
  await expect(list.getByRole('link')).toContainText([PROJECT.name, EMPTY_PROJECT.name])

    15	export function useResource<T>(key: string | null, load: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>, refreshToken = 0): { state: Resource<T>; reload: () => void } {
    16	  const [settled, setSettled] = useState<{ token: string; value: Resource<T> } | null>(null)
    17	  const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState(0)
    18	  const loadRef = useRef(load)
    19	  useEffect(() => { loadRef.current = load }, [load])
    20	  const token = key === null ? null : `${key}\u0000${attempt}\u0000${refreshToken}`
    21	
    22	  useEffect(() => {
    23	    if (token === null) return
    24	    const controller = new AbortController()
    25	    loadRef.current(controller.signal).then(
    26	      data => { if (!controller.signal.aborted) setSettled({ token, value: { status: 'ready', data } }) },
    27	      error => { if (!controller.signal.aborted) setSettled({ token, value: { status: 'error', error } }) },
    28	    )
    29	    return () => controller.abort()
    30	  }, [token])
    31	
    32	  const reload = useCallback(() => setAttempt(previous => previous + 1), [])
    33	  const state: Resource<T> = token === null ? { status: 'idle' } : settled?.token === token ? settled.value : { status: 'loading' }
    34	  return { state, reload }
    35	}

export function reviewSummary(review: ReviewResult): string {
  const { verdict, findings } = review
  if (findings.length === 0) return `${verdict} with no findings`
  const counts = DISPOSITIONS
    .map(disposition => [disposition, findings.filter(finding => finding.disposition === disposition).length] as const)
    .filter(([, count]) => count > 0)
    .map(([disposition, count]) => `${count} ${disposition}`)
  const blocking = findings.filter(isBlockingFinding).length
  return `${verdict} with ${findings.length} ${findings.length === 1 ? 'finding' : 'findings'}: ${counts.join(', ')}, ${blocking === 0 ? 'none blocking' : `${blocking} blocking`}`
}

=== PR11 handoff: UI/test claims ===
3:Implements `docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md` and its three slice PRDs on branch `ultra` (worktree `~/dev/md-manager-ultra`), 2026-09-21. All three slices were implemented directly in this checkout rather than as feature runs; the feature directories `features/review-result/` and `features/run-inputs/` and the `launch` choices the PRDs ask for exist, so the runs can still be launched, but nothing in the tree depends on them. Commits are left to the user. Section 6 lists what was deliberately not done.
21:- UI: review panel on the review node (verdict pill, reviewer session and transport, bundle hash linked to the candidate node, summary line, findings grouped by disposition, "Diff the reviewer saw"), "no review recorded" for legacy runs; mocks (worker phase) and seeds (candidate phase); scenarios `review-verdict`, `review-blocked`, `review-legacy`, `paths-redacted`.
28:- UI: Assignment tab and run-header facts, worker node panels (Task with Rendered/Source toggle and highlight, Exact prompt, Launch receipt, Reported by the worker, Handoff as accepted, Stop confirmation), finding quotes linking to the worker's task scrolled to the highlighted quote; scenarios `run-assignment`, `worker-inputs`, `finding-to-task`, `inputs-legacy`, `inputs-paths-redacted`.
30:## 2. How it was built and audited
32:The contract (`contracts/projects/v1.ts` 1.2.0, `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`) and a design spec pinning the export format were written first; three workstreams (controller, adapter, UI) were then implemented in parallel against them, each red-first, and merged. After the merged tree was green, an adversarial audit ran six independent read-only lenses over the uncommitted diff against the PRDs (controller protocol, adapter security, export-shape consistency, PRD completeness, UI and browser tests, Python test honesty); the lenses reproduced their claims with scratch probes and mutation runs. Every finding was verified by hand and fixed (section 6 lists the behavioural ones): redaction gaps next to Markdown punctuation and `file://` URIs, a finding link that could point past the served text's truncation, a check-ID rule that would have hidden a whole workflow behind one `test:unit` policy, an invented reviewer transport for pre-slice-A plans, an interrupted native review projecting as pending, a false RUNBOOK claim about `attach`, a Ctrl-C in the reviewer launch window that stranded the session, a post-acceptance stop that was never retried, the unlinked diff `uri`, a vacuous browser assertion, an unrecorded deviation on findings grouping, and five untested guards (identity, independence, worktree and evidence re-checks, print-mode `worker`/`requirement`, best-effort pane, launch-failure receipt). Guard removals were confirmed to fail their new tests on scratch copies. The live smoke tests in section 4 found the two launch-time defects (variadic option order, permission-rule family) that neither the offline tests nor the audit could see.
34:## 3. Gates run from the repository root (final pass, 2026-09-21 21:40 UTC, after the audit fixes)
43:| Browser suite, worker phase: `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts` | 15 passed (6 before), 0 skipped |
44:| Browser suite, candidate phase (`WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate`, real adapter with seeded runs) | 15 passed, 0 skipped |
49:- Adapter: eight tests failed for the expected reasons against the old adapter (a 1.2.0 export was `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID`, the new routes were `NOT_FOUND`), then 28/28; two audit-driven tests (redaction spellings, served-text links, policy-label IDs, null transport; interrupted review projects as paused) brought it to 30/30.
50:- Controller: the workstream reported behavioural reds per increment (fake reviewer through `FakeSessions`, four-process reviewer-interrupt recovery, every rejected completion file, print fallback), then 108/108; the audit fixes added 15 tests (launch-window interrupts, stop retry, identity/independence/worktree/evidence refusals, print-mode finding fields, best-effort pane, launch failure, `attach` reviewer pane, recorded transport) and one prompt test, 124/124, with guard removals confirmed red on scratch copies.
51:- UI: the nine new scenarios failed first for behavioural reasons (no tablist, no task panel, no findings rows, no not-recorded sentences) with the six existing ones passing, then 15/15 in both phases; the audit fixes (group-by toggle, pinned receipt assertions, diff link by ID) kept both phases at 15/15.
52:- Live smoke test (slice A section 5), scratch run built from a copy of project-workflows-001's bundle, diff and packets with the review node driven on its own:
59:  - The reviewer's eight findings concern the already-merged candidate b5385b3 (the Projects viewer feature), not this change set; they are retained in the scratch run's `review.json` for the operator: event normalisation only emitting status/log events, phase-conditional assertions in the run-evidence scenario, thin regression coverage of the Pi/Claude experience, per-request packet loading in `listRuns`, one malformed run directory making a whole workflow unbrowsable, inconsistent redaction in `projectWorkerResult`, the app-wide `frameworkErrors` handler, and event-derived attempt numbers. Several restate the print-mode reviewer's earlier findings.
74:- `automatic.reviewer_transport` is nullable: the export records the transport the plan pinned, or the one a recorded review actually used, and null for a run pinned before the setting that never reviewed; it never defaults to `native` (an audit found the earlier default contradicted `review.transport` for project-workflows-001).
75:- Check and scenario IDs in `runInputs` are free-form policy labels (the policy schema allows any non-empty string, e.g. `test:unit`); an earlier draft required the route-ID pattern and would have hidden a whole workflow behind one such run.
76:- Audit-driven fixes after the first green run: redaction now covers paths adjacent to Markdown punctuation and `file://` URIs; a quote links only when it also survives in the served (truncated) task text; the viewer builds the diff link from the artifact ID like every other artifact; an interrupted native review projects as `paused` rather than `pending`; `attach` adds the reviewer pane to an existing tab; a Ctrl-C in the reviewer's launch window is resumable; the post-acceptance stop is retried on resume; the identity/worktree/evidence re-checks, print-mode `worker`/`requirement` recording, the best-effort pane and the launch-failure receipt are now covered by tests.
77:- Not done: no fuzzy requirement matching (verbatim only); no live streaming; no viewer controls; the feature runs `review-result`/`run-inputs` were not launched.

content.thinking: All four medium findings check out on re-reading, with the duplicate inputs panels issue actually broader than initially stated, and the spot-checked praise items also hold up. Writing up the verdicts now.

verdicts.title: Helper extraction to support.ts left projects.spec.ts with a full duplicate set
verdicts.reason: projects.spec.ts in PR 11 differs from main by only 9 lines (two extra fixture imports, a run-list count 3->5, two data-status assertions, and a /results/ filter in run-evidence); lines 30-64 still define runUrl, apiRun, workspace, graphNode, nodeListItem, nodeDetail, expectNoExecutionControls, attach, waitForProjectsApi and a local test.beforeEach, with no import from ./support.ts. support.ts:14-50 defines the same ten names and review.spec.ts:18 / inputs.spec.ts:22 import them. The execution-controls regex exists verbatim in both files.
verdicts.evidence: `diff main/tests/project-workflows/projects.spec.ts ultra/.../projects.spec.ts` -> hunks only at 18a19, 19a21, 140c142, 143a146-147, 192c196-197. `grep -rn 'approve|retry|launch' tests/project-workflows/` -> support.ts:28 and projects.spec.ts:46 (identical regex). projects.spec.ts:34 `const runUrl = ...`, :35 `const apiRun = ...`, :44 `async function expectNoExecutionControls`, :61 `test.beforeEach(`; support.ts:17 `export const runUrl`, :26 `export async function expectNoExecutionControls`, :44 `export function installHooks()`.

verdicts.title: Third copy of the tab keyboard handler, and it focuses through a data-testid selector
verdicts.reason: RunView.tsx:66-77 onTabKey is the same if/else chain as DocumentView.tsx:95-106 and Editor.tsx:124-135 (ArrowRight/Down, ArrowLeft/Up, Home, End, preventDefault, setTab). The only divergence is the focus line: the two existing copies use `tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()` (DocumentView:105, Editor:134) with refs assigned at DocumentView:167 / Editor:170, while RunView:76 does `event.currentTarget.parentElement?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`[data-testid="${TABS[next].testId}"]`)?.focus()`. Functionally it works (inputs.spec.ts:85-88 asserts ArrowLeft focuses the Run tab), so this is a quality issue, not a bug. Note the two-copy duplication predates PR 11; the new part is the third copy and the testid coupling. Medium is defensible: a reviewer would ask for refs (or a shared hook) before merge.
verdicts.evidence: ultra src/projects/RunView.tsx:66-77; main src/document/DocumentView.tsx:95-106 (`tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()` at :105) and src/document/Editor.tsx:124-135 (:134); `grep -rn 'role="tablist"\|onTabKey\|tabRefs' src/` on main shows tabRefs only in the two document components.

verdicts.title: Duplicate loading and error panels for the one inputs resource
verdicts.reason: True and slightly broader than stated. The run header block (RunView.tsx:81-120) is rendered outside the tab switch (tabs start at :122, panel choice at :142), and it renders `LoadingPanel`/`ErrorPanel` for `inputs` at :102-103. NodeDetail.tsx:241-242 renders the same two panels for the same `inputs` prop on worker nodes, and Assignment.tsx:22-23 renders them a third time on the Assignment tab. ErrorPanel (panels.tsx:22) is `role="alert"` with a Retry button (:28). So a failed inputs fetch produces two alerts and two Retry buttons on a worker node, and also two on the Assignment tab.
verdicts.evidence: RunView.tsx:102 `{(inputs.status === 'loading' || inputs.status === 'idle') && <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}`, :103 `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={reloadInputs} />`; NodeDetail.tsx:241-242 `{isWorker && ... <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}` / `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={onRetryInputs} />`; Assignment.tsx:22-23 same pair; panels.tsx:22 `<div className="projects-error" role="alert" ...>`, :28 `<button ...>Retry</button>`.

verdicts.title: ui-task tells the UI worker to link required checks to executed checks 'with the same id', but executed checks have no id
verdicts.reason: PR 10's required-check schema carries `id`, `kind`, `command`, `timeout_seconds`, `scenarios` (contracts/projects/v1.ts:92-98). Executed checks in the worker result use `checkSchema` from contracts/workflow/v1.ts, which PR 10 leaves byte-identical to main: `command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id`, no `id`. Nothing in PR 10's run-inputs README names a join key (grep for check/verbatim/link only finds the scenario row and the JSON example). The instruction at ui-task.md:14 therefore cannot be followed literally; a worker must either infer `command` as the key or stop under the 'stop and report' rule. PR 11 resolved the same question explicitly (contract comment v1.ts:106; its ui-task.md:15 says 'a check whose command equals an executed check's command').
verdicts.evidence: PR 10 features/run-inputs/ui-task.md:14 'each check id links to the executed check with the same id in the node's worker result when one exists'; PR 10 contracts/projects/v1.ts:92-98 `checks: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: id, kind: ..., command: z.string().min(1), timeout_seconds, scenarios }))`; `diff <(awk checkSchema main) <(awk checkSchema high)` -> identical: `command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id`; PR 11 contracts/projects/v1.ts:106 '/** The approved argv joined exactly as the verifier records executed commands, so check IDs can be matched to executed checks. */'.

input.ranking_note: PR 11 is the only PR with UI and browser tests to judge, and what it ships holds up under re-reading: 15 scenario ids each appear in exactly one test title with exactly one screenshot attachment (grep count), the two new specs contain no phase conditionals or skips (grep returned nothing), assertions are exact (summary strings, per-group counts, class/attr/href, diff bytes fetched from inside the page, ArrowLeft focus, in-viewport poll on the mark, highlight cleared on leaving), the candidate seed includes a genuine 1.0.0 export (seed.ts:257-274) so the on-disk live-run shape is proven to load in both phases, and fixtures thread a `leak` argument that the candidate seed fills with a real absolute path (seed.ts:140-142) so adapter redaction is exercised for real. The mark tokens compute to 12.4:1 (light) and 5.8:1 (dark). The three confirmed quality/design defects are real and one is broader than reported (inputs Loading/Error is rendered in three places, so both the worker node and the Assignment tab show two role=alert panels), plus four rendered states have no test coverage; none is a correctness bug. That keeps it at 8, not higher. PR 10 delivers a specification only; it is internally consistent (policy descriptions were updated when paths-redacted widened to inputs, every cited contract name exists) but one deliverable is unimplementable as written (required-check id vs id-less executed checks) and it ships nothing runnable on this dimension, so 6. PR 9 changes nothing under src/, tests/project-workflows/ or features/*/ui-task.md; its 1 is the floor of the scale and a statement of scope, not quality.

new_findings.title: Candidate seed carries a real 1.0.0 export, so the live run's shape is proven to load in the browser
new_findings.detail: RUN_LEGACY is seeded as `version: '1.0.0'` with `values.review` present but no review/inputs section, which is exactly the shape of the existing project-workflows-001 run on disk (1.0.0 export plus a print-mode review.json). review-legacy and inputs-legacy then assert `projects-error` count 0, `result-unscoped` count 0 and the explicit not-recorded sentences on the run header, the Assignment tab and a worker node, in both phases. Combined with the `leak` parameter (fixtures default to `<path>`, the candidate seed substitutes a real path under the temp root), the redaction and legacy scenarios test the real adapter rather than the mock's own output.
new_findings.evidence: seed.ts:256-274 `// Integrated before review results and run inputs were exported: a 1.0.0 export ...`, `review: { run_id: RUN_LEGACY, verdict: 'approved', ... }`, `version: '1.0.0'`; seed.ts:140-142 `function leakFor(runsRoot, runId) { return join(runsRoot, runId, 'worktree-ui', 'test-results') }`; fixtures.ts:348 `uiPathQuote = (leak = PATH_TOKEN) => ...`, :445 `reviewFindings(runId, leak = PATH_TOKEN)`; review.spec.ts:139-153 and inputs.spec.ts:226-249 assert not-recorded states with `projects-error` toHaveCount(0).

new_findings.title: Four rendered states have no browser assertion, and reviewer transport is asserted by loose substring
new_findings.detail: The components expose testids for the truncated-task note, the missing launch receipt, an empty findings list and a highlight quote that is not found in the task, but no spec references any of them. The Assignment tab has a dedicated `assignment-reviewer-transport` testid, yet run-assignment only asserts `toContainText('native')` on the whole panel, which would also pass on any other occurrence of that substring.
new_findings.evidence: Loop over data-testids in ReviewDetail/WorkerInputs/Assignment/RunView grepped against tests/project-workflows/*.spec.ts -> UNTESTED: findings-empty (ReviewDetail.tsx:163), launch-none (WorkerInputs.tsx:133), task-highlight-missing (WorkerInputs.tsx:60), task-truncated (WorkerInputs.tsx:57), assignment-reviewer-transport (Assignment.tsx:39); inputs.spec.ts:61 `await expect(assignment).toContainText('native')`.

new_findings.title: UI hard-codes the `launch_<lane>` graph naming convention as a fallback for finding links
new_findings.detail: When run inputs are not loaded, `launchNodeFor` guesses the launch node for a lane by probing the pinned definition for a node literally named `launch_<lane>`, else falls back to the lane id. It is commented and only a fallback, but it encodes a graph-authoring convention in the viewer that the contract does not promise.
new_findings.evidence: ReviewDetail.tsx:49-56 `/** The graph node that launched a lane: from the inputs when loaded, else `launch_<lane>` when the pinned graph has it, else the lane itself. */ ... return definitionNodes.some(candidate => candidate.node_id === `launch_${lane}`) ? `launch_${lane}` : lane`.

verdicts.title: Third copy of the tab keyboard handler, and it focuses through a data-testid selector
verdicts.reason: RunView.tsx:66-77 onTabKey is the same if/else chain as DocumentView.tsx:95-106 and Editor.tsx:124-135 (ArrowRight/Down, ArrowLeft/Up, Home, End, preventDefault, setTab). The only divergence is the focus line: the two existing copies use `tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()` (DocumentView:105, Editor:134) with refs assigned at DocumentView:167 / Editor:170, while RunView:76 does `event.currentTarget.parentElement?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`[data-testid="${TABS[next].testId}"]`)?.focus()`. Functionally it works (inputs.spec.ts:85-88 asserts ArrowLeft focuses the Run tab), so this is a quality issue, not a bug. Note the two-copy duplication predates PR 11; the new part is the third copy and the testid coupling. Medium is defensible: a reviewer would ask for refs (or a shared hook) before merge.
verdicts.evidence: ultra src/projects/RunView.tsx:66-77; main src/document/DocumentView.tsx:95-106 (`tabRefs.current[next]?.focus()` at :105) and src/document/Editor.tsx:124-135 (:134); `grep -rn 'role="tablist"\|onTabKey\|tabRefs' src/` on main shows tabRefs only in the two document components.

verdicts.title: Duplicate loading and error panels for the one inputs resource
verdicts.reason: True and slightly broader than stated. The run header block (RunView.tsx:81-120) is rendered outside the tab switch (tabs start at :122, panel choice at :142), and it renders `LoadingPanel`/`ErrorPanel` for `inputs` at :102-103. NodeDetail.tsx:241-242 renders the same two panels for the same `inputs` prop on worker nodes, and Assignment.tsx:22-23 renders them a third time on the Assignment tab. ErrorPanel (panels.tsx:22) is `role="alert"` with a Retry button (:28). So a failed inputs fetch produces two alerts and two Retry buttons on a worker node, and also two on the Assignment tab.
verdicts.evidence: RunView.tsx:102 `{(inputs.status === 'loading' || inputs.status === 'idle') && <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}`, :103 `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={reloadInputs} />`; NodeDetail.tsx:241-242 `{isWorker && ... <LoadingPanel>Loading the run inputs…</LoadingPanel>}` / `<ErrorPanel error={inputs.error} what="The run inputs" onRetry={onRetryInputs} />`; Assignment.tsx:22-23 same pair; panels.tsx:22 `<div className="projects-error" role="alert" ...>`, :28 `<button ...>Retry</button>`.

verdicts.title: ui-task tells the UI worker to link required checks to executed checks 'with the same id', but executed checks have no id
verdicts.reason: PR 10's required-check schema carries `id`, `kind`, `command`, `timeout_seconds`, `scenarios` (contracts/projects/v1.ts:92-98). Executed checks in the worker result use `checkSchema` from contracts/workflow/v1.ts, which PR 10 leaves byte-identical to main: `command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id`, no `id`. Nothing in PR 10's run-inputs README names a join key (grep for check/verbatim/link only finds the scenario row and the JSON example). The instruction at ui-task.md:14 therefore cannot be followed literally; a worker must either infer `command` as the key or stop under the 'stop and report' rule. PR 11 resolved the same question explicitly (contract comment v1.ts:106; its ui-task.md:15 says 'a check whose command equals an executed check's command').
verdicts.evidence: PR 10 features/run-inputs/ui-task.md:14 'each check id links to the executed check with the same id in the node's worker result when one exists'; PR 10 contracts/projects/v1.ts:92-98 `checks: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: id, kind: ..., command: z.string().min(1), timeout_seconds, scenarios }))`; `diff <(awk checkSchema main) <(awk checkSchema high)` -> identical: `command, cwd, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, log_artifact_id`; PR 11 contracts/projects/v1.ts:106 '/** The approved argv joined exactly as the verifier records executed commands, so check IDs can be matched to executed checks. */'.
